 Two popular children’s products sold online are being recalled because of serious safety risks, and federal officials say the products could put kids at risk for injury or even death.
 SLIDE PLAYSETS 
 The U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission urged people to stop using Arlopu Slide Playsets and X-VESOLJE Nursing Pillows after finding they create dangerous situations for young children.
 Arlopu Slide Playsets with model numbers KT-CS17 and LY-31 are being recalled because they have several openings that can trap a child’s head or neck. The basketball nets on model KT-CS17 can also come unhooked and create a loop big enough for a child’s head, which can lead to entanglement or strangulation hazards. Arlopu received one report of a child getting abrasions on the neck due to becoming trapped on the playset.
 The playsets are made of plastic, designed for indoor or outdoor use and include a slide and basketball hoop. They were sold in tan, red, blue, yellow, gray and green. KT-CS17 is printed on a label under the elevated platform and LY-31 appears on a label on the upper back panel behind the slide.
 Officials say families should stop using the playsets immediately and store them where children cannot reach them. Those who own one should contact Arlopu at 800-657-9218 between 9 a.m. and 5:30 p.m. Eastern Time on weekdays or email arlopu_support@163.com. Consumers will need to send a photo of the model number and then Arlopu will mail a free repair kit with redesigned parts and new installation instructions. After completing the repair, families are asked to label removed parts as "RECALLED" and throw them away.
 NURSING PILLOWS 
 X-VESOLJE Nursing Pillows are being recalled by Kikea Store after they were found to violate key safety rules for nursing pillows. The CPSC said the pillows can block an infant’s breathing, leading to a serious risk of suffocation. The recalled pillows are model NP001 and are C-shaped. They come in patterns including white with leaves, dark brown with multicolored feathers and multicolored puzzle pieces. The products do not have any labels or markings.
 The CPSC urged consumers to stop using the pillows right away and contact Kikea Store at zsally929@gmail.com for a full refund. Shoppers will need to send in a photo after cutting the pillow in half and then throw out the destroyed product.
 Federal officials warned that it is illegal to sell or resell any of these recalled products. The CPSC has spent more than 50 years working to keep families safe from dangerous products and encourages families to quickly follow recall instructions to prevent further harm.
